'''''Juniperus squamata''''', the '''flaky juniper''', or '''Himalayan juniper''' is a [[species]] of [[conifer]]ous shrub, or sometimes small tree, in the cypress [[family (botany)|family]] [[Cupressaceae]], [[native species|native]] to the [[Himalayas]] and [[China]]. 

It represents the provincial tree of [[Khyber Pakhtunkhwa]] (unofficial).

==Description==
It is an [[evergreen]] [[shrub]] (rarely a small [[tree]]) reaching {{Convert|2–10|m|ft|abbr=off|frac=2}} tall (rarely 15 m), with flaky brown [[Bark (botany)|bark]], and a prostrate to irregularly-conical crown. The [[leaves]] are broad, needle-like, {{Convert|3–9|mm|frac=8}} long, arranged in six ranks in alternating whorls of three, and often strongly a glaucous blue-green in color. The [[conifer cone|cones]] are berry-like, globose to ovoid, 4–9 mm long, and 4–6 mm diameter. Often, they are a glossy black and contain one [[seed]]; they are mature in about 18 months. The male cones are 3–4 mm long and shed their pollen in early spring. It is largely [[dioecious]], with pollen and seed cones produced on separate plants, but occasionally [[monoecious]].<ref name=adams/><ref name=farjon/><ref name=foc/>

==Taxonomy==
Three to five [[Variety (botany)|varieties]] are accepted, with treatment differing between different authors:<ref name="adams" /><ref name="farjon" /><ref name="foc" />
*''Juniperus squamata'' var. ''squamata'' – leaves mostly 5–9 mm. Throughout the standard range.
*''Juniperus squamata'' var. ''fargesii'' Rehder & E.H.Wilson – leaves mostly 3–5 mm. Confined to the eastern half of the range in China.
*''Juniperus squamata'' var. ''hongxiensis'' Y.F.Yu & L.K.Fu; often included in var. ''squamata''.<ref name="adams" />
*''Juniperus squamata'' var. ''parviflora'' Y.F.Yu & L.K.Fu; often included in var. ''squamata''.<ref name="adams" />

''[[Juniperus morrisonicola]]'' {{small|Hayata}} from Taiwan is often treated as a [[synonym (taxonomy)|synonym]],<ref name="farjon" /> or a variety ''Juniperus squamata'' var. ''morrisonicola'' (Hayata) H.L.Li & H.Keng,<ref name="gd">Gymnosperm Database: [http://www.conifers.org/cu/ju/squamata.htm ''Juniperus squamata'']</ref> but is better treated as a distinct species as it has a distinct DNA profile.<ref name="adams" />

=== Etymology ===
The Latin [[Botanical name#Binary name|specific epithet]] ''squamata'' means small, scale-like leaves.<ref name=RHSLG>{{cite book|last=Harrison|first=Lorraine|title=RHS Latin for gardeners|year=2012|publisher=Mitchell Beazley|location=United Kingdom|isbn=978-1-84533-731-5|pages=224}}</ref>

==Distribution and habitat==
It is found in (and native to) northeastern Afghanistan east to western Yunnan in southwestern China, with disjunct populations north to western [[Gansu]], east to [[Fujian]], and [[Taiwan]]. Recently, however, it was introduced to the United States in 1964 after being exported from the Netherlands.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Blue Star juniper - Juniperus squamata 'Blue Star' - PNW Plants |url=http://www.pnwplants.wsu.edu/PlantDisplay.aspx?PlantID=266 |access-date=2022-05-29 |website=www.pnwplants.wsu.edu}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=flaky juniper - Encyclopedia of Life |url=https://eol.org/pages/1061622 |access-date=2022-05-29 |website=eol.org}}</ref> It grows at altitudes from {{Convert|1,600 to 4,900|m|abbr=on}}.<ref name=adams>Adams, R. P. (2004). ''Junipers of the World''. Trafford. {{ISBN|1-4120-4250-X}}</ref><ref name=farjon>Farjon, A. (2005). ''Monograph of Cupressaceae and Sciadopitys''. Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew. {{ISBN|1-84246-068-4}}</ref><ref name=foc>Flora of China: [http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=2&taxon_id=210000925 ''Juniperus squamata'']</ref><ref name="iucn status 12 November 2021" />

==Cultivation==
''Juniperus squamata'' is widely grown as an [[ornamental plant]] in Europe and North America, valued for its bluish foliage and compact habit. The following cultivars have gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]]:<ref>{{cite web  | url= https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/pdfs/agm-lists/agm-ornamentals.pdf | title = AGM Plants - Ornamental | date = July 2017 | page = 56 | publisher = Royal Horticultural Society | access-date = 14 March 2018}}</ref> 
*'Blue Carpet'<ref>{{cite web|title=RHS Plant Selector - ''Juniperus squamata'' 'Blue Carpet'|url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/74874/Juniperus-squamata-Blue-Carpet/Details|publisher=Royal Horticultural Society|access-date=26 September 2020}}</ref> 
*'Blue Star'<ref>{{cite web|title=RHS Plant Selector - ''Juniperus squamata'' 'Blue Star'|url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/99002/Juniperus-squamata-Blue-Star/Details|publisher=Royal Horticultural Society|access-date=26 September 2020}}</ref> 
*'Holger'<ref>{{cite web|title=RHS Plant Selector - ''Juniperus squamata'' 'Holger'|url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/80428/Juniperus-squamata-Holger/Details|publisher=Royal Horticultural Society|access-date=26 September 2020}}</ref>
